mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 0.5% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 6% signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 falls by more than 0.5% and UNRATE exceeds 6%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of at least 100,000 for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 100,000 for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of four consecutive months of 100,000+ PAYEMS increases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and increases recession risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during three consecutive months of >0.5% INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) and Real Personal Savings (RSAFS) signals increased household investment and liquidity, which supports consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both rise month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both HOUST and RSAFS rise month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.4% month-over-month while the federal funds rate remains below 2%, it indicates an inflation surprise under accommodative policy, which erodes purchasing power and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: loose monetary policy with rising inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during months with CPIAUCSL > 0.4% MoM and FEDFUNDS < 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% for six consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of six consecutive months with UNRATE below 5%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (GDPC1) of more than 0.8% quarter-over-quarter, accompanied by a stable unemployment rate (UNRATE change within ±0.1%), signals robust demand growth without labor market overheating, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 QoQ > 0.8% AND UNRATE change within ±0.1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during quarters with GDPC1 > 0.8% QoQ and UNRATE change within ±0.1%.
